definitions.explanation: Fertilizer derived from natural, organic materials such as compost, animal manure, bone meal, or plant matter, as opposed to chemically synthesized fertilizers.

examples.japanese: {有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}を{使|つか}って{野菜|やさい}を{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: I grow vegetables using organic fertilizer.

examples.japanese: {有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}は{土|つち}の{質|しつ}を{改善|かいぜん}する{効果|こうか}がある。
examples.english: Organic fertilizer has the effect of improving soil quality.

examples.japanese: {化学|かがく}{肥料|ひりょう}の{代|か}わりに{有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}を{選|えら}ぶ{農家|のうか}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More farmers are choosing organic fertilizer instead of chemical fertilizer.

notes:
A compound of {有機|ゆうき} (organic) and {肥料|ひりょう} (fertilizer). Increasingly common as interest in organic farming ({有機|ゆうき}{農業|のうぎょう}) and sustainable agriculture grows in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}を{施|ほどこ}す: to apply organic fertilizer
- {有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}で{栽培|さいばい}する: to cultivate with organic fertilizer
- {完熟|かんじゅく}{有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}: fully composted organic fertilizer

TYPES:
- {堆肥|たいひ}: compost — decomposed plant matter
- {鶏糞|けいふん}: chicken manure
- {骨粉|こっぷん}: bone meal
- {油|あぶら}かす: oil cake; seed meal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {化学|かがく}{肥料|ひりょう}: chemical fertilizer — the synthetic counterpart
- {堆肥|たいひ}: compost — one specific type of organic fertilizer
- {肥|こ}やし: fertilizer; manure — more colloquial general term
